parsedVerdict.reasoning: The infrastructure module is one cohesive adapter concern. It holds persistence adapters (in-memory-repositories.ts) that implement the domain repository interfaces, an HTTP adapter (order-controller.ts) that delegates to the application services, and the composition root (server.ts) that wires them together. The controller always goes through OrderService and CatalogueService and never reaches the repositories directly, so the module's abstractions are used consistently. Input validation (isState, orderId) and error mapping (handle) each live in one place inside the module. One minor concern: order-controller.ts redefines the valid OrderState values as a runtime array. This repeats the domain's union type, and if the domain gains a state the compiler won't flag that the array is missing it. Because a runtime check at the HTTP edge is a normal adapter job and the domain source isn't shown (so a bypass of an existing domain constant can't be confirmed), I treat this as a weak concern, not a violation. OrderController also serves the /products routes, so its name is narrower than its responsibility, but it is still a single HTTP adapter.
